speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe if your double vision improves when you close one eye, and do you experience any numbness or tingling in your limbs? Additionally, have you noticed any recent muscle weakness in your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Given your symptoms of diplopia (double vision) on upgaze and proximal weakness, I need to check your pupil reaction. Please cover one eye and tell me if the double vision persists. Also, can you try to hold your arms up in front of your face as high as possible for as long as you can?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
